h1: The 7 Best Small Safes for Apartments of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Small Safes for Apartments: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 small safes for apartments scored on mounting, lock type, capacity and renter-friendly setup, from Bonsaii to Master Lock.
summary: The Bonsaii 0.6 cubic foot safe is the apartment safe to buy: a removable shelf, two mounting holes with expansion screws and three ways to open it, including a USB-C backup. The KornerBatl 20 lb biometric safe needs no mounting at all, and the Master Lock 5900D tethers by cable for renters whose lease bans any drilling.
intro: A small safe in an apartment is as much a lease problem as a security problem. Bolting a safe to a wall or floor is the single best way to stop someone walking off with it, and it is also exactly what many landlords forbid. The honest question is not which safe is strongest, but which one you can install without losing your deposit.

We ranked seven small safes in the under $25 to $100 range and scored them on the Primea framework, weighting installation and mounting options most heavily, then lock design, capacity, power backup and price. Safe ratings and certifications are rarely stated on these listings, so we did not assume any. Treat all of these as deterrents against casual theft, roommates and curious children.

products.name: Bonsaii Safe Box with Electronic Keypad for Home Office, 0.6 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: The roomiest anchored option, with a removable shelf and three ways to open it.
products.description:
Bonsaii's 0.6 cubic foot safe holds more than anything else here that bolts down, and includes a removable shelf for organising passports, jewellery and a laptop. Two mounting holes and expansion screws are included, and you can open it with a keypad, a key or a USB-C backup.

It ranks first because it combines the best capacity with a real anchor option, in the $50 to $100 bracket. The USB-C backup covers the nightmare of a dead battery, which is a common failure of keypad safes. The tradeoff is the mounting: to use the holes you must drill, which a strict lease may forbid, and it is bulkier than the 0.23 cubic foot models.

A fit for renters who are allowed to anchor. Others should consider the KornerBatl.
products.idealFor: Renters who may anchor and want space for mixed valuables.
products.skipIf: Your lease bans drilling into walls or floors.

products.name: KornerBatl 20 lb Biometric Safe with Fingerprint Lock & LED Light
products.verdict: A 20 lb safe whose weight deters carry-away, with fingerprint, keypad, key and Type-C power.
products.description:
KornerBatl's biometric safe weighs 20 lb, which is its anti-theft feature: a casual intruder cannot pocket it. It offers four ways in, fingerprint, keypad, key and Type-C power, plus an LED light and a silent mode that keeps beeps down in thin-walled apartments.

It ranks second because it solves the no-drilling problem with mass instead of mounting, and the silent mode is a thoughtful apartment detail. Against the Bonsaii 0.6, it cannot be anchored in the listing, so a determined thief with a vehicle can still carry it off. Fingerprint readers also fail with wet or dirty hands, which is why the keypad and key backups matter.

A good pick for renters with a no-alteration lease. Keep a spare key somewhere separate.
cons: Can still be carried by a determined thief
products.idealFor: Renters with a no-drill lease who want fast access.
products.skipIf: You want a safe you can bolt to the structure.

products.name: Small Safe for Home, 6.69"H Safe Box with Fireproof Waterproof Bag
products.verdict: A compact box with an alarm, three unlocking methods and a bag for documents.
products.description:
This 10.63 by 6.69 by 6.69 inch safe has optional concealed anchoring, an alarm with a mute mode, three ways to unlock it that prevent a single point of lockout, and a bag for documents, all for under $50.

Third place rests on the alarm and three unlocking methods suit shared apartments where roommates or guests are the actual threat, and the compact body hides easily in a closet. The fireproof bag is stated, but the listing does not give a fire rating for the safe itself, so keep expectations modest. Against the Bonsaii models, it is cheaper but smaller and less documented.

A fair match for roommate situations. Store documents in the bag, not loose.
cons: No fire rating for the box stated
products.idealFor: Shared apartments where roommates are the concern.
products.skipIf: You want a verified fire rating.

products.name: Bonsaii Small Safe Box with Electronic Keypad for Valuables, 0.23 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: A 0.23 cu ft keypad safe with USB-C backup and pre-drilled holes for easy patching.
products.description:
The smaller Bonsaii holds 0.23 cubic feet with a small mounting footprint, pre-drilled installation holes and USB-C emergency power, for under $50.

Fourth place makes sense for the compact version of the best safe here, trading the 0.6 model's shelf and room for a lower price and a smaller hole to patch at move-out. A two-hole mount is easier to fill than a larger anchor pattern. The keypad plus USB-C backup suits renters who dread a dead battery. Next to Voncabay, the USB-C backup is the differentiator.

A good option for a small collection of documents and jewellery. Expect only pocket-sized storage.
products.idealFor: Small collections of documents and jewellery.
products.skipIf: You need to store a laptop or larger items.

products.name: Voncabay Money Safe Box for Home with Digital Keypad, 0.23 Cu. Ft., Black
products.verdict: A mountable steel box that locks out for 5 minutes after three wrong codes.
products.description:
Voncabay offers a 0.23 cubic foot mountable steel box with a digital keypad that locks out for 5 minutes after three wrong entries, an automatic interior light and a low-battery warning, again for under $50.

Fifth place is earned by the lockout is a real defence against children and curious roommates guessing codes, and the interior light helps in dark closets. Against the Bonsaii 0.23, it lacks the USB-C backup, so a dead battery means using the key or a screwdriver, which the listing does not detail. The low-battery warning reduces that risk.

A decent choice for a bedroom closet with kids around. Replace the batteries at the first warning.
products.idealFor: Closets where kids or guests might try to guess a code.
products.skipIf: You want an emergency power port.

products.name: Master Lock Small Travel Safe with Cable, Gray Combination Lock Box, 5900D
products.verdict: A tethered travel safe with a 4-digit combination and no drilling at all.
products.description:
The Master Lock 5900D is a small combination lock box with a tether cable, a 4-digit code with no key to lose and a charging cable access port. It requires no wall or floor drilling and sells under $25.

It ranks sixth because a cable is a deterrent, not a vault: bolt cutters defeat it, and the box itself is small. The listing names the strict-lease use case directly, and the tether lets you loop it around a pipe or a bed frame. Its charging port is a niche feature that lets a phone charge inside the safe. Compared with the KornerBatl, it is cheaper but offers only casual security.

A good fit for renters who cannot alter anything, and for travel. Choose a code you can remember.
products.idealFor: Renters whose lease forbids any alteration, and travellers.
products.skipIf: You need real resistance to a determined thief.

products.name: Yuanshikj Small Steel Security Safe Box with Keypad, Key, 0.23 CuFt, Black
products.verdict: A 0.23 cu ft steel box with keypad, key and a magnetic auto-lock door, at the lowest price.
products.description:
Yuanshikj sells a small steel security box of 0.23 cubic feet with a keypad, a key and a magnetic auto-lock door, in the under $25 tier. The mounting footprint is small, so patching it at move-out is easy.

Seventh place reflects a bare-bones page: no emergency power port, no lockout feature and no alarm. The magnetic auto-lock is convenient, since the door locks itself as it closes, but that is also the only standout. Against the Voncabay it costs less and gives up the lockout and light.

A budget way to keep documents away from visitors. Do not rely on it for high-value items.
products.idealFor: Keeping documents and small items away from visitors.
products.skipIf: You want protection for high-value items.

whatMatters.detail: Anchoring a safe to a wall or floor is the best defence against carry-away, but many leases ban drilling. Check your lease before buying. If you cannot drill, choose weight, like the 20 lb KornerBatl, or a tether, like the Master Lock. Look for pre-drilled holes and the size of the patch you will need at move-out.

Keypad safes run on batteries, and a dead battery without a backup can lock you out. USB-C emergency power or a physical key solves it. Check how many ways the safe opens, and whether the listing names an emergency method. Fingerprint readers work well but can fail with wet hands, so a second method matters.

0.23 cubic feet holds documents, a passport, a few small items and jewellery, while 0.6 cubic feet fits a laptop and papers. Measure your largest item and compare it with the interior dimensions in the listing, not the outside size. Remember that shelves and foam linings reduce usable space.

Thin apartment walls make beeping keypads annoying at night. A silent mode lets you open the safe quietly, and an alarm can deter roommates. Check whether the listing names a mute or silent setting, and whether the alarm can be turned off, so it does not wake the household by accident.

None of these listings state a burglary or fire rating, so treat them as deterrents against casual theft, roommates and children. A fireproof bag is a bag, not a certified safe. For irreplaceable documents, keep copies elsewhere, and consider a rated safe or a bank box if the contents justify the cost.

faq.q: Can I install a safe in a rental without losing my deposit?
faq.a: Often yes, with a small mount. The Bonsaii 0.23 has pre-drilled holes that are easy to patch. If drilling is forbidden, choose the 20 lb KornerBatl or the tethered Master Lock instead.

faq.q: What mistake do renters make with small safes?
faq.a: Leaving them unanchored and light. A small box like the Yuanshikj can be picked up and carried away, so either bolt it down or choose a heavy one such as the KornerBatl.

faq.q: Is the Bonsaii 0.6 worth it over the 0.23?
faq.a: If you can anchor and need space, yes. The 0.6 adds a removable shelf and room for a laptop, while the 0.23 is cheaper, fits tight closets and leaves a smaller patch when you leave.

faq.q: How do I set up a keypad safe?
faq.a: Install fresh batteries, set a code that is not your birthday and test it with the door open. On the Voncabay, remember it locks out for 5 minutes after three wrong codes.

faq.q: How do I avoid being locked out?
faq.a: Keep the key in a separate place and replace batteries at the first warning. The Bonsaii models accept USB-C emergency power, and the Voncabay gives a low-battery warning before it fails.

faq.q: Will a small safe protect papers from fire?
faq.a: Do not assume so. The Small Safe for Home includes a fireproof bag, but the listings give no fire rating for the boxes themselves. For irreplaceable papers, keep copies in a second location.

finalTake: For most apartments the Bonsaii 0.6 cubic foot safe is the right buy: roomy, with mounting holes included and a USB-C power backup. If your lease bans drilling, the 20 lb KornerBatl is the best answer, with the Master Lock 5900D as the cheap tether. Shared housing suits the alarm-equipped Small Safe for Home, and the Voncabay suits kids.
